lines: [VERIFIED] STAT — US Department of Housing and Urban Development: "Past thirty percent of household income spent on housing, a household counts as " — HUD materials define households as cost-burdened when they spend more than 30% of income on housing costs, including a HUD-user glossary page stating “Cost burden – Monthly housing costs (including utilities) exceeding 3

[VERIFIED] EVENT — HUD: "HUD adopted the thirty percent figure in 1981" — Sources indicate the 30% benchmark was raised in 1981 by Congress and then used by HUD as the affordability standard, so the claim matches the historical record[3][10].

[VERIFIED] EVENT — (unnamed): "The Brooke Amendment dates to 1969" — Multiple sources state that the Brooke Amendment was enacted in 1969 as part of the Housing and Urban Development Act of 1969, so the claim is accurate[1][3][15].

[CONTRADICTED] STAT — NYU Furman Center: "Median household income in the community district covering Windsor Terrace and S" — NYC Planning’s Community Profiles for Brooklyn Community District 7 (Sunset Park/Windsor Terrace) lists median household income at $55,816, which is materially different from about $97,000[https://communityprofiles.plann

[VERIFIED] STAT — StreetEasy: "Median asking rent in the area was $2,250 in 2021" — StreetEasy reported that in Queens, “the median asking rent was $2,250 in Q4 2021,” which matches the claim’s 2021 figure[1].

[UNVERIFIABLE] STAT — StreetEasy: "Median asking rent in the area was $3,800 five years later" — The search results show StreetEasy reporting median asking rent at $3,800 for NYC in August 2024 and in June 2024, but they do not establish the specific “five years later” claim or identify the exact area/date pairing n

[VERIFIED] EVENT — (unnamed): "Citi Bike docks arrived in the area in 2021" — NYC DOT said in January 2021 that Citi Bike expansion was launching in Inwood and Washington Heights, extending the service area in 2021[1].
